title: Three small numbered round flasks and one clear flask in a white perforated circular laboratory vessel
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the image.

Three small round-bottom glass flasks with narrow necks and glass stoppers are visible on the perforated platform inside the circular vessel; each small flask contains a grey/brown slurry and has a handwritten black number on its body.

One larger clear glass flask (appears to be an Erlenmeyer- or conical-shaped vessel) containing a clear liquid is present at the right side of the perforated platform inside the same circular vessel; the larger flask has a small handwritten letter 'G' on its side.
The white circular vessel (a round chamber with a removable perforated tray) is visible, including a black circular seal or O-ring set into its upper rim.
Supporting bench surface and a vertical metal rod or pipe are visible adjacent to the circular vessel but are not counted as numbered equipment.

The three small round-bottom flasks form a roughly triangular arrangement toward the left and center of the perforated tray: the flask labeled '2' is at the upper-left region of the tray, the flask labeled '5' is toward the upper-center/back of the tray, and the flask labeled '3' is toward the front-center of the tray.
The larger clear flask marked 'G' is positioned at the right side of the perforated tray, partly occupying two nearby perforation holes.
A black rubber-like O-ring runs around the inner rim of the chamber above the perforated tray.
A vertical metal rod or pipe is visible outside the chamber at the upper-left edge of the image, and the chamber sits on a dark bench surface that runs across the bottom of the image.
